Evidence: AC-07 has two different meanings; AC-08..10 exist only in CSV.
Impact: Two conflicting acceptance baselines can cause different interpretations of MVP completion and test evidence.
Recommended Action: Choose one source of truth, reconcile IDs, link every criterion to test/evidence and make chapter 02 reference the register.

Evidence: All 42 FR rows use the same generic Acceptance Evidence placeholder; no explicit AC IDs or Test IDs/source paths/evidence commits.
Impact: FR completion cannot be independently verified or change impact traced.
Recommended Action: Add BR/NFR/AC/Test ID/code path/commit/run/evidence/status/deviation fields for every FR.

Evidence: New ST/PR/IN/OR invariant IDs are not mapped one-to-one to original BR IDs or tests.
Impact: A business rule can disappear or change meaning during model refactoring without visible trace.

Evidence: The diagram combines OrderStatus, FulfillmentStatus and PaymentStatus although the text says they are separate.
Impact: Ambiguous completion, cancellation, delivery and COD transitions may lead to inconsistent order workflows.
Recommended Action: Create separate state models and define cross-state policies, actors, invariants and tests.

Evidence: Idempotency lookup occurs before transaction; diagram does not show atomic key claim, unique-conflict handling or concurrent duplicate path.
Impact: Concurrent retries with the same key may race unless a unique constraint/atomic claim closes the gap.
Recommended Action: Claim the idempotency key atomically inside the transaction with a unique constraint and explicit conflict/replay behavior.

Evidence: No complete ERD or column-level Data Dictionary; current schema and target commerce schema are not presented as separate complete artifacts.
Impact: Data model, EF mappings, SQL constraints and future commerce entities may diverge during implementation.
Recommended Action: Publish Current ERD from migrations and Target ERD separately; add SQL types, nullability, keys, indexes, defaults, deletes and migration strategy.

Evidence: Rev2.0 gives compact UC summaries; it does not preserve full preconditions, trigger, numbered success path, alternate/error flows, postconditions and linked rules/tests for each use case.
Impact: Teams cannot use the catalogue as a complete implementation and test contract.
Recommended Action: Keep summaries in the handbook and restore detailed per-UC specifications with FR/BR/AC/Test links.

Evidence: Context diagram treats Public Catalog Read API as if external to RetailFlow and places database outside without container semantics; container diagram is a layer flowchart, not a precise C4 container view.
Impact: System boundaries and internal/external responsibilities may be misunderstood.
Recommended Action: Redraw true Context/Container/Component views; keep Current/Target distinction and describe each boundary/technology/relationship.

Evidence: 16 controls are high-level statements without exact ASVS requirement IDs, applicability, test IDs or evidence links.
Impact: The project cannot claim measurable ASVS coverage or security acceptance from the matrix.
Recommended Action: Map applicable ASVS 5.0.0 requirements to component, implementation, test, evidence and approved exception.

Evidence: P95/P99, load, tenant scale, availability, RPO/RTO, retention and cost objectives remain unresolved.
Impact: Performance, resilience and recovery gates cannot be objectively passed or failed.
Recommended Action: Obtain owner-approved measurable Quality Attribute Scenarios and SLO/RPO/RTO/retention targets; do not invent values.

Evidence: Phase G Product Host Foundation is labeled Current slice but its baseline status is Target despite implemented Product Host/catalog slice in the code.
Impact: Roadmap misstates progress and weakens evidence-based phase reporting.
Recommended Action: Set G to Implemented/Partially Implemented with source and CI links; keep deferred capabilities in later phases.

Evidence: The file reports commit status pending/no entries; GitHub Actions Run #10 and its Build, SQL Integration & Playwright E2E Check Run on the same SHA completed successfully.
Impact: The baseline evidence record is incomplete and can mislead reviewers.
Recommended Action: Record traditional Status API separately from Check Runs; link Run ID 45623148657 and exact SHA.

Evidence: Master chapter 21 contains a reference-status addendum that is absent from the standalone chapter file.
Impact: The master and Docs-as-Code source can drift and publish different reference guidance.
Recommended Action: Generate the master from chapter sources or add an automated content sync/diff gate; one source of truth only.

Evidence: OpenAPI is 3.1.1 while 3.2.1 is the latest published specification as of 2026-11-25; no compatibility rationale is recorded and generic 500 responses are not described.
Impact: Potential toolchain compatibility lag and incomplete error contract documentation.
Recommended Action: Document compatibility decision, validate against generated host contract, and add shared ProblemDetails responses where applicable.

Evidence: SQL Server service password is fixed plaintext in the workflow. It appears limited to an ephemeral CI SQL container, not a production secret.
Impact: A reusable test credential may be copied into an unintended environment or normalized as a secret-handling pattern.
Recommended Action: Generate a per-run disposable password and ensure it is not reused outside ephemeral CI.
